Bug_Title: RV: Bad attempt to compute absolute value of signed 32-bit hashcode (RV_ABSOLUTE_VALUE_OF_HASHCODE)
Bug_Details:
This code generates a hashcode and then computes
the absolute value of that hashcode.  If the hashcode
is Integer.MIN_VALUE, then the result will be negative as well (since
Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE).
 One out of 2^32 strings have a hashCode of Integer.MIN_VALUE,
including "polygenelubricants" "GydZG_" and ""DESIGNING WORKHOUSES".
 Integer.MIN_VALUE Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the line where the absolute value of the hashCode is calculated. If the hashCode is Integer.MIN_VALUE, then the result will be negative as well, since Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) == Integer.MIN_VALUE.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by passing the string 'DESIGNING WORKHOUSES' to the showBug method which has Integer.MIN_VALUE as its hashCode. This causes Math.abs(hashCode) to return a negative value which then fails the assertion in the test case.
